vignette: Thanh is a 31-year-old male of Southeastern Asian descent, married with no children. His occupation as a judge requires him to maintain composure and rationality even in the most trying circumstances. Despite this professional demeanor, Thanh has been grappling with persistent anxiety and intrusive thoughts following a devastating typhoon that struck his hometown last year. Thanh vividly recalls the day when the sky turned ominously dark, and the winds howled with an intensity he had never experienced before. He was visiting family for a holiday when the storm made landfall, and it quickly became clear that this was no ordinary weather event. The wind shattered windows and uprooted trees as if they were toothpicks, and the rain came down in sheets, making visibility almost nonexistent. Thanh found himself trapped in his aunt's house, which began to shake violently under the onslaught of the storm. Memories of the howling winds and shattering glass are etched in his mind, often replaying themselves during the quiet moments of his day. In his role as a judge, Thanh is usually meticulous about his work and decisions, but lately, he has found it difficult to concentrate on cases. The loud bangs and sudden gusts from the courthouse air conditioning remind him of that stormy night, causing his heart rate to spike and his palms to sweat. He frequently checks the weather forecast multiple times a day, even when there is no indication of any severe storms in the vicinity. This constant vigilance has taken a toll on both his professional performance and personal relationships. At home, Thanh's wife notices that he seems more on edge than usual. Simple noises like thunder or heavy rain can trigger vivid flashbacks that leave him feeling disoriented and distressed. He often finds himself looking out windows to ensure there are no dark clouds gathering, a ritual that has become part of his daily routine. Thanh acknowledges these behaviors but feels helpless in stopping them; the fear of another storm is overwhelming. During the nights, Thanh struggles with sleep, haunted by nightmares where he relives the intensity of that typhoon. He wakes up drenched in sweat and breathless, struggling to convince himself that it was just a dream. His wife has grown concerned about his exhaustion and has suggested seeking professional help, but Thanh is hesitant. As someone who relies on logic and order, the idea of being unable to control these intrusive thoughts and feelings is deeply unsettling. Thanh's marriage has also been affected by his condition. He finds it challenging to engage in everyday conversations without drifting into memories of that fateful day. His wife understands his fears but sometimes feels excluded from their shared life. They have started spending less time together, as Thanh often avoids going out or engaging in activities they both once enjoyed. Despite these challenges, Thanh continues to perform admirably at work. He believes that maintaining this façade of composure is essential for his professional credibility and personal pride. However, the strain of living with constant reminders of the typhoon weighs heavily on him. The memories and anxiety have become a constant companion, making it difficult for Thanh to fully engage in any activity without feeling an underlying sense of dread. Thanh's condition has gradually begun to affect his daily life, but he remains hopeful that with time and perhaps some support, he can regain control over his thoughts and emotions. The trauma from the typhoon is a stark reminder of the power of nature and the fragility of human resilience.
